source_text:
Ὅταν γὰρ τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ὑποτάσσησθε ὡς Ἱησοῦ Χριστῷ, φαίνεσθέ μοι οὐ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ζῶντες, ἀλλὰ κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τὸν δἰ ἡμᾶς ἀποθανόντα, ἵνα πιστεύσαντες εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ἐκφύγητε.
ἀναγκαῖον οὖν ἐστίν, ὥσπερ ποιεῖτε, ἄνευ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μηδὲν πράσσειν ὑμᾶς, ἀλλ’ ὑποτάσσεσθαι καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ὡς τοῖς ἀποστόλοις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῆς ἐλπίδος ἡμῶν, ἐν ᾦ διάγοντες εὑρεθησόμεθα.
δεῖ δὲ καὶ τοὺς διακόνους ὄντας μυστηρίων Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ κατὰ πάντα τρόπον πᾶσιν ἀρέσκειν. οὐ γὰρ βρωμάτων καὶ ποτῶν εἰσιν διάκονοι, ἀλλ’ ἐκκλησίας θεοῦ ὑπηρέται: δέον οὖν αὐτοὺς φυλάσσεσθαι τὰ ἐγκλήματα ὡς πῦρ.
thought_title: Submission to bishop, elders, and deacons
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Tralles, urging them to live in unity under their bishop, council of elders, and deacons.
pass_a_gloss: For whenever [you] to the bishop submit as to Jesus Christ, [you] appear to me not according to man living, but according to Jesus Christ the [one] for us having died, in order that having believed into the death of him the to die [you] might escape. Necessary therefore it is, just as [you] do, without the bishop nothing to do [for] you, but to submit also to the council of elders as to the apostles of Jesus Christ of the hope of us, in whom living [we] will be found. It is necessary also the deacons being of mysteries of Jesus Christ in every manner to all to please. For not of foods and drinks they are deacons, but of church of God servants: necessary therefore [for] them to guard themselves from the accusations as fire.

choices.why: The glossary and argument center on submission to the bishop; 'submit' keeps the force of the middle voice and the hierarchical relation.
The articular infinitive with the aorist subjunctive expresses purpose; 'escape dying' preserves the infinitive's verbal force rather than turning it into a noun.

choices.term: ἄνευ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μηδὲν πράσσειν ὑμᾶς
choices.english: that you do nothing without the bishop
choices.why: The accusative and infinitive construction after 'necessary' is rendered as a that-clause; 'do nothing' keeps the strong negation.
rejected: you should do nothing apart from the bishop
to do nothing without the bishop

choices.english: of the mysteries of Jesus Christ
choices.why: The genitive plural 'mysteries' is kept as a noun phrase; it refers to the sacred rites and teachings, not just secret knowledge.
rejected: of the secret things of Jesus Christ
of the sacraments of Jesus Christ

choices.why: The comparative 'as fire' implies guarding against accusations with the same urgency as guarding against fire; 'as against fire' makes the protective stance explicit.

pass_b_english: When you submit to the bishop as you would to Jesus Christ, it is clear to me that you are not living in a merely human way. You are living according to Jesus Christ, who died for us so that by believing in his death you might escape death itself.

So it is necessary, as you are already doing, that you do nothing without the bishop. Submit also to the council of elders as you would to the apostles of Jesus Christ our hope, in whom we will be found if we live in him.

The deacons, since they serve the mysteries of Jesus Christ, must please everyone in every way. They are not deacons of food and drink, but servants of the church of God. They must therefore guard themselves against accusations as they would guard against fire.

problems.quote: in whom we will be found if we live in him
problems.why: Source says 'in whom living we will be found,' not conditional 'if we live.'
problems.fix: in whom, as we live, we shall be found.

edits.old: in whom we will be found if we live in him
edits.new: in whom, as we live, we will be found

last_rejected.fix: deacons of the mysteries of Jesus Christ
last_rejected.ruling: Source says διακόνους...ὄντας; 'servants' renders διάκονος fine here, no glossary conflict.

last_rejected.fix: guard themselves against blame as against fire
last_rejected.ruling: ἐγκλήματα = 'accusations/charges'; 'guard against accusations' is valid, context doesn't demand 'faults'.

polish.changed: Clarified the parallel between the bishop and Christ, and between the council of elders and the apostles; made pronoun references explicit; smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud.

notes.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

notes.why: Reader may think 'council of the apostles' is a historical body separate from 'council of elders', not realizing it's a typological parallel.
notes.fix: Add note: 'council of the apostles' typologically parallels 'council of elders'.

notes.quote: council of elders of the church

variants.text: council of elders of the church

notes.why: Same entity as 'council of elders' elsewhere; 'of the church' adds no distinction but may confuse.
Same office rendered two ways; readers may think 'elders' are different from 'council of elders.'

polish.changed: Clarified the opening clause so the comparison to Jesus Christ is explicit, smoothed the transition between sentences, and kept the deacons' warning vivid and direct.

notes.why: Same Greek word (presbyterion) rendered as 'council of elders' but also 'council of the bishop' and 'council of the apostles', which may confuse readers about whether these are the same body.
notes.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; note 'council of the apostles' is a different metaphor.

notes.why: In 2.6, elders stand 'in the place of the council of the apostles'—but 'council of the apostles' is not the same as 'council of elders', though both use 'council'. Reader may conflate them.
notes.fix: Clarify that 'council of the apostles' is a separate metaphor for the apostolic college.

notes.why: Unique phrase 'council of the bishop' in 5.8; elsewhere always 'council of elders'. Reader may wonder if this is a different body or a mistake.
notes.fix: Verify Greek; likely should be 'council of elders' or add note explaining this variant.

notes.why: Same office rendered four ways; 'council of God' and 'council of the bishop' could be mistaken for different bodies.
notes.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; reserve 'apostles' for the apostles.
